text: China should have five time zones.
It's more than five thousand kilometres wide, and the sun takes four hours to cross it.
Until nineteen forty-nine, China really had five.
Then the whole country was put on Beijing time.
On a winter morning, the sun rises over Shanghai before seven.
Then it keeps going west, for hours,
until it finally reaches Kashgar, after ten a.m.
So many people there quietly keep their own clock, two hours behind.
Would you wait until ten for the sunrise?
